expectations.text: Explains conditional certification: possible only if the assessment score is at least 88 (0.8 x 110) AND every NOT MET practice is POA&M-eligible
expectations.evidence: "To be eligible for a POA&M-based conditional certification, an organization generally must: 1. Have no unmet POA&M-ineligible practices... and 2. Achieve a minimum overall SPRS-equivalent score threshold at the time of the initial assessment — historically set at 88 out of 110 points as the floor for POA&M eligibility." Both conditions (score ≥88 and all-eligible) are stated, despite hedging language.

expectations.text: States POA&M eligibility rules correctly: only practices worth 1 point may be on a POA&M (no 5-point items; 3-point items excluded except limited partial-credit cases), and names non-POA&M-eligible critical examples (e.g., SC.L2-3.13.11 FIPS crypto, AC.L2-3.1.3, IA.L2-3.5.3)
expectations.evidence: Response only vaguely gestures at the rule: "items worth 5-point deductions were more likely to be excluded from POA&M eligibility" and states "the remaining practices — generally the lower-weighted ones (1-point and some 3-point deductions) — are eligible to be POA&M'd," which contradicts the correct 1-point-only rule (3-point items are excluded except limited partial-credit cases). No specific practice IDs (e.g., SC.L2-3.13.11, AC.L2-3.1.3, IA.L2-3.5.3) are named anywhere in the response.

expectations.text: States the closeout: POA&M items must be remediated and verified by a closeout assessment within 180 days, or the conditional certification lapses
expectations.evidence: "You have a fixed window — historically 180 days — to remediate all POA&M items and undergo a POA&M Closeout Assessment, which verifies the previously NOT MET (now remediated) practices are actually implemented... If you fail to close out within the window, the conditional certification expires."

expectations.text: Explains the consequence math for THIS scenario: 8 NOT MET practices are compatible with conditional certification only if all 8 are 1-point items and the score floor holds — otherwise remediate and re-assess
expectations.evidence: Response only says generically "calculate your actual point deduction total based on the specific weight of each of your 8 NOT MET practices (1, 3, or 5 points each depending on the practice) and confirm you're at or above the 88-point floor." It never ties this to the specific requirement that all 8 must be 1-point items (having earlier stated some 3-point items can also be POA&M-eligible), and never performs the concrete math (e.g., 8 x 1pt = 102) for this scenario.

expectations.text: Notes the July 13, 2026 context accurately: with Phase 2 suspended pending the task-force review, C3PAO certification mechanics are described under the rule as written while acknowledging new C3PAO-designated requirements are in abeyance; the annual senior-official affirmation in SPRS continues, and a lapsed conditional status affects contract eligibility
expectations.evidence: No mention anywhere in the response of July 13, 2026, the Phase 2 suspension, the CMMC Reform Task Force review, or the annual senior-official affirmation. The response treats CMMC Phase 2/C3PAO certification as fully active with no caveat about the current suspension.
